data.title: 1inch Tells Resolver Delegators to Claim Rewards and Undelegate by November 27
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, 1inch has urged staking users who delegated to resolvers to claim their rewards and complete undelegation by November 27. The newly added resolver delegation channel is closed. The change does not affect regular 1INCH staking, and users who stake independently do not need to undelegate or migrate.

data.title: Anonymous Address Adds $18.99 Million in BTC Shorts, With $35.69 Million in Total Losses
data.description: An unidentified address’s futures account has accumulated losses of about $35.69 million and increased its BTC short position by 282.42 BTC, valued at about $18.99 million. According to Odaily, the address currently holds a 282.42 BTC short position and opened BTC shorts worth about $16.81 million. The address is 0x1f250df59a777d61cb8bd043c12970f3afe4f925.

data.title: Honda Recalls 14,648 Vehicles in U.S. Over Brake Pressure and Crash Risks
data.description: According to Jin10, Honda is recalling 14,648 vehicles in the United States because a loss of brake pressure could reduce braking ability, increase stopping distances, and raise crash risk.

data.title: Cosmos Hub Proposal 1061 Surpasses Voting Threshold to Fix Governance Query Issue
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Cosmos Hub Proposal 1061 to fix a governance query issue has entered the voting stage, surpassed the quorum threshold, and received near-unanimous support. If approved, validators will need to upgrade their nodes to Gaia v29.1.0 at block height 33,935,300.

data.title: STOCKS | LFG+Zest CIO Alberto Conca: U.S. Tech Under Pressure, European Stocks Hold Up as Market Breadth Widens
data.description:
According to Jin10, LFG+Zest Chief Investment Officer Alberto Conca said the breadth of the market rally is widening and defensive European equities may continue to outperform. Conca made this assessment before a change in Nvidia’s leadership.

Information technology accounts for more than 35% of the MSCI USA Investable Market Index, compared with 8.8% of the corresponding European index. European indexes have greater exposure to financials, health care and energy, while earnings at some companies and better-than-expected economic data have also provided a buffer.

That protection is relative. Investors say Europe’s lower technology weighting can cushion volatility in a single sector, but stocks in Europe and other regions could also be dragged down if a selloff spreads from U.S. technology shares to the broader Wall Street market.

data.title: Hong Kong Man in His 70s Loses HK$17.2 Million in Crypto Investment Scam
data.description:
A Hong Kong man in his 70s lost about HK$17.2 million in a cryptocurrency investment scam. According to Foresight News, citing reports by Oriental Daily, the man left his contact details through a YouTube investment advertisement in June this year and was contacted by a fraudster posing as an investment adviser. He was added to a WhatsApp group and, following the adviser’s instructions, opened an account to buy and trade virtual currencies.

From August to October, he transferred USDT and ETH worth more than HK$18 million to digital wallets provided by the scammers. After his son noticed suspicious activity in early October, the man tried to withdraw his funds and retrieved only about HK$800,000 worth of USDT. The platform then rejected further withdrawal requests, leaving him with a net loss of about HK$17.2 million. Hong Kong police received more than 40 investment fraud reports over the past week, with total losses approaching HK$50 million.

data.title: stUSDT Begins Orderly Exit, Redemption Portal to Close May 14, 2027
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing DefiLlama, stUSDT and wrapped wstUSDT, tokens operating on Tron and Ethereum, have begun an orderly exit. The official announcement says rebase rewards ended on November 14, 2026, when the redemption window opened. The portal will close at 7:59 PM (U.S. Eastern Time) on May 14, 2027. DefiLlama data showed stUSDT’s total value locked at about $9.49 million on November 14, down from $60.28 million a year earlier. The exit guide does not state the reason for the wind-down or specify redemption rates or fees; the team says underlying assets remain fully backed. Holders must move tokens from exchanges or platforms such as JustLend, SunSwap, and Curve to a personal Web3 wallet. stUSDT holders must unstake and claim USDT on the official site; wstUSDT holders must unwrap first. After the deadline, requests will be submitted through official customer support and processed in monthly batches through August 2027. Wallets need TRX or ETH for network fees.

data.title: Elon Musk Says Cybercab’s Self-Driving Subscription Fee Is Too High
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Tesla has opened Cybercab purchases to a limited group of invited customers, with a starting price of $29,990 and first deliveries expected in December. Buyers must pay a $1,000 deposit and subscribe to the self-driving service for $299 per month. Musk said the monthly fee is too high and should be comparable to the roughly $115 charged for other Tesla models.

data.title: Ethereum Community Publishes Draft EIP for General-Purpose Proof Verification and Batching
data.description: The Ethereum community has published a draft EIP for general-purpose proof verification and batching. According to Foresight News, the proposal would enable LEANSTARK_SCHEME, which was reserved by EIP-8288, and introduce general-purpose proof verification and sponsored batch proofs. A sponsor could pay collectively for an aggregation node containing multiple claims, while members would pay for the claims they submit. Any valid subset of claims could be included without requiring new signatures. The draft also specifies verifier identity, resource limits, dependency digests, and activation thresholds based on performance benchmarks.

data.title: U.S. Democrats Ask Musk to Preserve Starlink Speed-Limit Records After Jensen Huang Draws Scrutiny
data.description:
Two Democratic U.S. senators have written to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, asking him to preserve all records concerning restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starlink and Starshield. According to Odaily, Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons called restrictions affecting Ukraine in October and November “unsettling,” and said the vulnerabilities could exist in systems used by the U.S. government. They said the issue raised serious questions about SpaceX’s control of communications systems critical to national security and asked Musk to provide written confirmation by November 30 that all appropriate safeguards had been implemented.

Starshield, developed by SpaceX as a military version of Starlink, primarily serves the U.S. government and military. Ukraine has reported multiple times since October that aircraft equipped with Starshield terminals lose connectivity when traveling faster than 160 kilometers per hour, disrupting several military missions. Musk has said the U.S. government controls Starshield and that restrictions on speed or use are determined by the U.S. military, ultimately depending on U.S. President Donald Trump. Trump has denied involvement in the speed limits.

data.title: Blackstone’s AirTrunk Files Plans for $11 Billion India Data Center Campuses
data.description: Blackstone’s AirTrunk filed detailed plans for two hyperscale data center campuses in southern India that could involve about 1.03 trillion rupees ($11 billion) in investment, according to Bloomberg. The project is among India’s biggest proposed digital-infrastructure developments.

data.title: Alliance Co-Founder Imran Khan: Crypto VCs May Join Frontier Tech After 1–2 Cycles
data.description:
Alliance co-founder Imran Khan said a recent LP dinner included a discussion about whether crypto venture capital firms are still needed. According to Foresight News, participants generally agreed they are, but perhaps for only one or two more cycles, after which crypto may become fully integrated into the broader frontier technology market. Khan described this as a positive sign of the industry’s maturation, saying the wider technology market has validated the value created by crypto.

From a fund perspective, Khan said the range of crypto-only opportunities has narrowed since 2020, making it difficult for large funds to generate scalable returns through crypto alone. Expanding into areas such as robotics and physical AI is therefore a logical step. While younger technology talent is moving toward AI and robotics, Alliance data show that more existing crypto talent is leaving large companies to start independent ventures. LPs are not bearish on crypto, Khan said, but see long-term opportunities in its convergence with newer fields.

data.title: Trezor Cuts Distributor Network by About 80%, Confirms Implants in 3 Safe 5 Devices
data.description:
Trezor confirmed on November 12 that three Safe 5 devices had hardware implants and said it had reduced its distributor network by about 80%. According to Odaily, the devices were sold by Malaysian distributor CryptoBilis from August 20 to September 23. The implant was a circuit board placed between the screen and motherboard that copied screen contents, including recovery phrases, then encrypted and sent the data over a mobile network to an attacker’s server. Because it did not alter the firmware or security element, routine checks were unlikely to detect it.

Firmware version 2.13.1, released on November 11, disabled the implants but cannot protect backups made before the update. Customers who bought through the distributor must move to wallets using new recovery phrases. Trezor said the network reduction was not due to a loss of trust in its partners. Customers who bought devices through the channel from March onward can request replacements. No customers had reported losses as of the report. The same distributor was also involved in a Ledger device-tampering case in which more than $86 million was stolen.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent Says He Moved to Military Base, Rebukes WSJ Over Address Disclosure
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC on the 13th that he had moved from his home to a military base, citing the Secret Service’s instructions and a Wall Street Journal photo of his residence that included geolocation information. He said the newspaper published the photo on the day he bought the house despite pleas to keep its location private, calling the decision “extremely irresponsible” and “very dangerous” and saying it must stop. Bessent also said Iran’s leadership had issued death threats against him, adding that this meant the “economic isolation” campaign was taking effect.

data.title: China and U.S. Hold First Meeting of Trade Council Under Economic and Trade Consultation Mechanism
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, China and the U.S. held the first meeting of the Trade Council under their economic and trade consultation mechanism by video conference on November 13. The sides discussed implementing outcomes from earlier consultations, including tariffs, a reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement involving $30 billion on each side, and agricultural trade. They said they would continue communicating through the Trade Council to address their respective economic and trade concerns.

data.title: Dario Amodei: Anthropic Is Not Focused on IPO Timing or Market Conditions
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said Friday during a fireside chat with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon at JPMorgan’s New York headquarters that the company is not particularly concerned about which month or market conditions it chooses for an IPO. He said Anthropic aims to “underpromise and overdeliver.”

Amodei said he agrees with the view that a company should not be valued even $1 above its true worth. Against recent volatility in the AI sector and pressure on technology stock valuations, Anthropic is taking a cautious approach to IPO pricing. The company is reportedly targeting a valuation of about $1.33 trillion or higher and plans to offer 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, which would raise more than $61 billion at the midpoint. Investors, including Google, also plan to invest about $26 billion through a private placement. Amodei called computing investment the company’s “deepest business challenge,” saying substantial spending on computing resources continues to pressure its finances.

data.title: Ecuador Seeks to Monetize Biodiversity While Continuing Amazon Oil Drilling
data.description: According to CNBC, Ecuador is pursuing new ways to finance nature conservation while planning to continue oil extraction in parts of the Amazon. The government hopes to issue its first sovereign green bonds in 2027 and is seeking advice from the European Union on the instruments, Environment and Energy Minister Juan Carlos Blum said. In March, IDB Invest and Banco Bolivariano issued a $120 million biodiversity bond to support conservation projects. Debt swaps completed in 2023 and 2024 freed up about $1.1 billion for conservation in the Amazon and Galapagos Islands. In October, the government announced plans to open new oil exploration tenders in parts of the Amazon, according to local media reports. Ecuador also plans to host the U.N. biodiversity summit, COP18, in 2028.

data.title: Aiden Pleterski Testifies He Was Kidnapped and Beaten
data.description:
Aiden Pleterski, who called himself the “Crypto King,” testified at Ontario Superior Court in Toronto on November 13 that he had been kidnapped and beaten. According to Foresight News, citing CBC, Pleterski described being held for three days in early December 2022, during which he said he was beaten, waterboarded and threatened with a gun.

The jury watched a video showing Pleterski on his knees pleading as a gunshot sounded near his ear. Akil Heywood, Alfredo Paladino and Rakeem Henry are charged with kidnapping and extortion; all three pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors allege that Heywood, a former investor, led the operation.

Last month, Pleterski was convicted of defrauding investors of more than CAD 30 million. He has not yet been sentenced, and the trial is expected to continue.

data.title: Ao Ying: Market Declines Still Offer Shorting Opportunities, Bitcoin Rallies Follow Corrections
data.description:
Crypto trader Ao Ying said market declines can still offer opportunities to profit from short positions. According to Odaily, allincrypto said on X that traders who believe hacking incidents, negative news about Strategy and Jensen Huang’s departure will continue to weigh on secondary markets can express that view by shorting. He said ongoing, unexpected events may offer clearer trading opportunities than some news that lags price movements.

Ao Ying said traders should distinguish normal stop-losses from emotionally driven decisions after losses. When a trade is based on sound reasoning, a timely stop-loss remains proper risk management even if the position loses money.

He also said negative events clustered in November, but a market decline can release risk and create more attractive price ranges. Past major Bitcoin rallies have often followed deep corrections, he said, adding that traders need not be overly pessimistic about the market’s next moves.

data.title: 58bro.eth Records $39.66 Million in Hyperliquid Profits After Selling 8,000 ETH and Buying Back 10,501
data.description: 58bro.eth has accumulated $39.66 million in profits on Hyperliquid, with an 87.5% win rate. According to Odaily, Lookonchain data shows that 58bro.eth sold 8,000 ETH at $2,397 one week ago and bought back 10,501 ETH over the past two days at an average price of $1,978.
